paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the God of Zion is worth bragging about, and the song says so right out loud. The sons of Korah open with "Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised…" (Psalm 48:1). Then they point to the kings who assembled and fled in terror, and they say "God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress" (Psalm 48:3-5). The safety of that city never came from its towers. It came from the One inside it.

The song doesn't want that to stay a fact on a page. It says "As we have heard, so we have seen," and then it turns to the temple, where the people "contemplate Your loving devotion" (Psalm 48:8-9). That's a good question for you, baker: have you only heard about God's loving devotion, or have you sat with it and seen it? Then comes a lap around the city, counting towers and touring citadels, so that you "may tell the next generation" (Psalm 48:12-13). What you learn about God is not just for you, friend. It's for somebody coming up behind you!

And look where the song lands: "For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death" (Psalm 48:14). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer thinking I'd been forgotten, so hearing "forever and ever" hits me right in the mustache. Whatever you're walking through today, this God doesn't hand you off to somebody shinier. He guides you the whole way, so go ahead and tell somebody about Him.
